heading: INT. GRAIN ELEVATOR - BASE LEVEL - NIGHT

units.text: INT. GRAIN ELEVATOR - BASE LEVEL - NIGHT
Dust hangs in the work light.
Conveyor belts, silent.
A hopper the size of a church.
CASIMIR "CASS" DUDA (40s, night foreman, canvas coat) walks the catwalk with a clipboard.
Counting bins.
Boots ring on steel.
Something shifts in the grain below.
Fenwick?
units.name: CASS

units.text: No answer.
He taps his flashlight against his palm.
FENWICK OKORO (20s, new hire, hard hat too big) climbs up from a ladder at the far end.
Wipes his hands on his overalls.
Looks pale.
Bin six is warm.
units.name: FENWICK

units.text: Grain heats. Settles.
units.name: CASS

units.text: It's breathing, Cass.
units.name: FENWICK

units.text: Cass hears it now.
A slow rattle, like a sleeper in the next room.
Cass swings his beam over the side.

Fenwick leans out beside him, and the grain below rises in a smooth dome, as if something is turning over under a blanket, and Cass grabs Fenwick by the collar while the light jumps across the rafters and a third person steps out from behind a support column, silent, in a yellow slicker.
The newcomer is MARGUERITE LAU (60s, inspector's badge, white braid).
She raises a hand for quiet.
Both of you. Back to the stairs. Walk.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: Who are you?
units.name: CASS

units.text: The reason this elevator was condemned in 1987.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: The dome in the grain sinks.
Slowly the rattle stops.
Is it gone?
units.name: FENWICK

units.text: It is listening.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: They walk to the stairs together, step for step, not looking back.
Behind them a single kernel rolls down the slope of the hopper and clicks against the steel.
